title: Move the lore check gate to lore 0.11.0 and re-export the .lore schemas
description: Observed 2026-09-27 at the close of the 0.11.0 release. The workstation lore is now 0.11.0, and `lore check` there reports 10 schema-drift errors: 8 committed schemas no longer match what the profile generates, and constitution and constants are declared types with no committed schema. CI is unaffected, because .github/workflows/lore-check.yml pins @opum-ai/lore@0.9.2 (line 140), so the required context stays green while a workstation check goes red. Same shape as QCLI-361 (lore 0.9.0): move the gate's pinned lore to the paired 0.11.0, run `lore schema export`, commit the schemas, and prove the gate both ways.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore-check.yml installs @opum-ai/lore@0.11.0, the version paired with quest 0.11.0 under Article 3
lore schema export is committed, and lore check exits 0 locally under lore 0.11.0 and in CI
The gate is proven both ways: clean green, and one deliberate violation red with a lore error, not a tooling error

plan: 2. Measure the regenerated tree under the old pin 0.9.2 via npx to choose one-PR vs two-step per the workflow header
3. Move the lore-check.yml pin to 0.11.0; lore check and lore agents --check exit 0
4. The PR CI going green on the new pin is the proof
implementationNotes: Measured 2026-09-27, workstation lore 0.11.0, quest 0.11.0. `lore schema export` under 0.11.0 restamped profileDigest on all eight committed schemas (sha256:a6d120fa... to sha256:2f362661..., one line each) and added constitution.schema.json and constants.schema.json. Under 0.11.0 the tree gives lore check exit 0, 63 files, 0 errors, and lore agents --check reads CLAUDE.md up-to-date. Under the OLD pin (npx @opum-ai/lore@0.9.2) the same tree exits 7: 8 schema-drift errors, plus schema-unattributable on the two new files. So neither order of two landings is green, and the regeneration and the pin move ship together in one PR. The workflow header said "two steps otherwise", which read as covering this case, so it is corrected in the same change. The managed quest block already declared 0.11.0, so it needed no regeneration (the relayed "0.7.1" is hand-written history prose at CLAUDE.md:603).
